ChatGPT said:

For your CDL Defense shield, you can make the gold star between CDL and Defense rotate continuously in 3D, just like a rotating gold coin, while keeping the rest of the shield completely still and the outer background transparent.

Since your website is built with React and CSS, I recommend using a separate transparent star image with a CSS 3D animation. This is more efficient than playing a video or GIF.

1. How the animation will look

Sketching the interface

Illustration of the 3D rotation effect.

2. Prepare your existing shield

The most important step is separating the star from your current image. You cannot independently animate an element that has already been flattened into a PNG.

  1. Open your shield in Photopea, a free browser-based image editor.

  2. Remove only the gold star between CDL and Defense, carefully reconstructing the red shield background underneath it.

  3. Save the star separately as star.png, with a transparent background.

  4. Export the shield without that star as shield.png, also with a transparent outer background.

This will preserve your original logo, colors, lettering and shield.

3. Add the animation to your React website

Once the two images are ready, place them in client/public/images/.

Use the following JSX:

JavaScript

import "./Shield.css";

export default function Shield() {
  return (
    <div className="shield-wrapper">
      <img
        src="/images/shield.png"
        alt="CDL Defense Shield"
        className="shield-image"
      />

      <img
        src="/images/star.png"
        alt=""
        className="rotating-star"
        aria-hidden="true"
      />
    </div>
  );
}

And the CSS:

CSS

.shield-wrapper {
  position: relative;
  width: min(100%, 500px);
  margin: 0 auto;
  perspective: 800px;
}

.shield-image {
  display: block;
  width: 100%;
  height: auto;
}

.rotating-star {
  position: absolute;
  width: 5%;
  height: auto;

  /* Adjust to match the original star position */
  left: 50%;
  top: 76%;

  transform-origin: center;
  transform-style: preserve-3d;

  animation: starRotate 3.5s linear infinite;
}

@keyframes starRotate {
  from {
    transform: translate(-50%, -50%) rotateY(0deg);
  }

  to {
    transform: translate(-50%, -50%) rotateY(360deg);
  }
}

@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  .rotating-star {
    animation: none;
    transform: translate(-50%, -50%);
  }
}

The star's position and width are initial estimates. Adjust them after exporting the two image layers to make sure the star fits naturally between the words.

4. For a more realistic 3D effect

If you want the star to have actual thickness, visible edges and realistic changing reflections as it rotates, use Blender. It can render a 3D gold star with transparent frames that you can use as a looping animation.

For your website, I would use the CSS approach first. It requires no extra libraries, keeps the rest of the shield stationary and doesn't introduce a large video file.

One important thing: To make the final result look professional, the star must be removed cleanly from the original shield. Simply placing an animated star over the existing one will leave the original star visible whenever the new star turns sideways.
